legend: Lentigo maligna melanoma characteristically has a prolonged radial growth phase, exemplified by this lesion, which was present for more than 15 years without a vertical growth phase.
This field shows the so-called classic pattern, with continuous basal (lentiginous) proliferation of uniformly atypical naevoid to epithelioid melanocytes.
Another field shows the dysplastic naevus–like (or naevoid lentigo maligna) pattern, although this single field is not diagnostic of lentigo maligna.

Predominantly basal proliferation of moderately and uniformly atypical naevoid to epithelioid and spindle melanocytes; there is focal low-level suprabasal scatter and there are a few nests that appear to hang down from the epidermis in a droplet-like pattern; the process is in situ in this field.

There is a collection of cells in the papillary dermis, filling and expanding it. The cells have a somewhat naevoid morphology (relatively small, scant cytoplasm), and there is evidence suggesting maturation to a smaller cell type at the base, but the nuclei are hyperchromatic and irregular. There are no mitoses; the invasive component in lentigo maligna melanoma is often somewhat naevoid, as in this case; the tumour thickness is 0.3 mm, indicative of a lesion at minimal risk of metastasis.
Clinical features of a lentigo maligna melanoma.

legend: Dermoscopic features. Minimally invasive lentigo maligna melanoma on the ala of the nose of a 90-year-old patient. Dermoscopy reveals grey-brown rhomboidal lines, asymmetrically pigmented circles, and grey dots.
source: By courtesy of Dr Iris Zalaudek

legend: Dermoscopic features. Invasive lentigo maligna melanoma on the ala of the nose of a man in his sixties. Note that the lesion represents a solitary spot on otherwise healthy-appearing skin. Dermoscopy reveals grey thickened lines around the hair follicles, grey dots, and diffuse ill-marked brownish pigmentation.
source: By courtesy of Dr Iris Zalaudek

diagnosis: Lentigo maligna and primary acquired melanosis of the conjunctiva
legend: Lentigo maligna / lentigo maligna melanoma involving the face, eyelid, and conjunctiva.
source: Drs R Barnhill and Nathalie Cassoux nathalie.cassoux@curie.fr

legend: Proliferation of atypical melanocytes at the dermoepidermal junction as confluent proliferation of single cells and nests. Extension along adnexal structures is seen. Underlying solar elastosis and mild infiltration of lymphocytes and melanophages are observed.
